definition: The Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus, a dataset of 800GB of English text collected from the web.
details: The Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus, a dataset of 800GB of English text collected from the web.

explainer.lead: C4, short for Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus, is an 800 GB collection of English text gathered from the web. It matters because it provides a large body of language material for work that needs English text at scale.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a gigantic library filled with English writing collected from websites. C4 is like that library, except its contents take up about 800 gigabytes of computer storage instead of sitting on shelves.
tiers.practitioner: Treat C4 as a large English text corpus and plan storage and processing around its 800 GB size. Check whether web-collected text fits the intended task; the corpus’s scale alone does not establish downstream quality.
tiers.paperLevel: C4 = Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus, an English-language text dataset collected from the web, with a stated size of 800 GB. It is a dataset rather than a model, algorithm, or evaluation metric; its definition specifies language, origin, and size, but not document count, task labels, or an evaluation protocol.

explainer.example: A researcher who needs a large sample of English writing could select a portion of C4 and process its text for a language study. C4 supplies the corpus, while the researcher must define the study’s method and any evaluation.

usedIn.name: Natural language processing
usedIn.detail: Provides a large collection of English text for language-focused work.

usedIn.name: Web-text research
usedIn.detail: Offers English text gathered from the web for corpus-based studies.

explainer.measures: C4 does not measure performance; it supplies English text collected from the web. Its stated scale is 800 GB.
howScored: There is no score associated with C4 itself. Any task results depend on the separate system or evaluation using the text.
caveats: The 800 GB figure describes data size, not document count or text quality.
Being collected from the web does not make the corpus representative of all English writing.
C4 is not a benchmark and provides no task score by itself.
